facts.v: Hemodialysis for diabetic nephropathy; end-stage renal disease.
Prior leadless pacemaker and drug-eluting stent in the left anterior descending artery for stable angina.
Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia complicated by infective endocarditis; receiving intravenous antibiotics.
Chest pain developed during treatment for the bloodstream infection.
Rapid hemodynamic deterioration with cardiogenic shock.
High inflammatory response; exact analyte values were not reported.
Disseminated intravascular coagulation was reported; exact values were not provided.
Echocardiography showed new left-ventricular wall-motion abnormalities and pericardial effusion, then tamponade.
After emergency pericardiocentesis, coronary angiography showed disruption of the prior stent and rapidly enlarging coronary pseudoaneurysm.
Optical coherence tomography and intravascular ultrasound showed loss of the arterial wall three-layer structure, consistent with pseudoaneurysm.
Emergency pericardiocentesis yielded yellowish, turbid pericardial fluid.
Surgical exploration of the leadless pacemaker revealed vegetation.
MRSA bacteremia was documented; exact culture sampling time and antimicrobial susceptibility details were not reported.

critical: Complicated infective endocarditis with coronary/pericardial involvement

cond: Acceptable for cardiogenic shock/tamponade after emergency stabilization; unit is not explicit in source.
Acceptable as immediate handoff for urgent coronary/pericardial source control, with critical-care monitoring.

facts.v: Two weeks after respiratory infection symptoms, dyspnea progressed to NYHA III with leg edema and abdominal pain; no chest pain or dizziness initially.
Ulcerative colitis controlled with mesalazine; past tobacco use.
Mesalazine.
Peripheral edema and bradycardia, heart rate 42/min.
No P waves; narrow-QRS escape rhythm at 42/min.
NT-proBNP 432 pg/mL (reference ≤125).
High-sensitivity troponin T 31 ng/L (reference ≤14).
D-dimer 2.94 µg/mL (reference <0.5 µg/mL).
TTE: preserved LV systolic function; dilated LA and RV; impaired RV function; severe tricuspid regurgitation; estimated systolic PA pressure 58 mm Hg; only mild mitral regurgitation.
CT pulmonary angiography: no pulmonary embolus; RV dilatation, bilateral pleural effusions and contrast reflux into hepatic veins.
Coronary CT: minimal proximal LAD stenosis only.
Right-heart catheterization: giant wedge V waves to 65 mm Hg, no clear A wave, mPAP 35, mean wedge 28 mm Hg, cardiac output 5.8 L/min, PVR 1.2 WU.
TEE confirmed only mild mitral regurgitation.
Cardiac MRI: left atrial late gadolinium enhancement and borderline T1/T2 edema; no substantial ventricular scar.
Subsequent study: electrically silent right atrium, limited septal capture and complete AV block; no response to coronary-sinus pacing.

critical: Clinically significant bradycardia or atrioventricular block
Atrial mechanical dysfunction with thromboembolic risk

cond: Urgency and phase aligned with published acute care

facts.v: Lumbosacral meningomyelocele; ileocecal augmented bladder and catheterizable stoma; later radical cystectomy for bladder cancer with continent MAINZ pouch I urinary diversion.
Increasing difficulty catheterizing for weeks; indwelling pouch catheter placed for continuous drainage. Drainage failed the night before presentation, with reduced urine output.
Severe lower abdominal pain and progressive dyspnea followed catheter dysfunction.
Cardiopulmonary decompensation on presentation; specific initial preoperative vital signs not reported.
Urgent contrast CT with retrograde pouch contrast: large left laterodorsal reservoir defect, contrast leakage into peritoneum and free intraperitoneal fluid.
Chest CT excluded pulmonary embolism and right-heart strain.
Before surgery: WBC 15.3×10^9/L, hemoglobin 143 g/L, platelets 513×10^9/L.
Before surgery: sodium 138 mmol/L, creatinine 1.08 mg/dL, eGFR 68 mL/min/1.73 m².
CRP 1.7 mg/L before surgery.
CRP 361 mg/L and procalcitonin 4.7 ng/mL on ICU day 2.
Postoperative ICU day 1 lactate 4.7 mmol/L.
Emergency laparotomy confirmed pouch rupture, which was repaired; pouch catheter fixed and nasogastric tube placed.
ICU after surgery: GCS 14, HR 120/min, systolic BP 110 mm Hg, SpO2 98% on 3 L oxygen; abdomen soft and moderately distended.
Two blood-culture sets on ICU day 2 remained negative after five days.
Drain fluid collected day 2 later grew low-quantity Klebsiella oxytoca; later sample grew vanB Enterococcus faecium.
Pouch urine on day 7 grew low-concentration Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
Research plasma microbial cfDNA identified Klebsiella and Pseudomonas retrospectively; result was not available for immediate care.

ICU day 2: pruritus, flushing, wheeze and agitation shortly after meropenem plus fluconazole; a second reaction followed piperacillin–tazobactam re-challenge. The offending component was not established.

critical: Acute urinary reservoir rupture with intraperitoneal leak/peritonitis and need for source control
acceptable: Ruptured continent urinary diversion pouch with intraperitoneal leak or peritonitis before later sepsis is established

cond: Acceptable immediate preoperative destination for urgent laparotomy.
Source-supported immediate postoperative destination after emergency repair.

facts.v: Two weeks of dyspnea and cough, briefly improved after an initial thoracentesis removed 1.5 L of milky right pleural fluid; recurrent dyspnea led to an ED return days later. No recent trauma or thoracic surgery.
45 pack-year smoking history.
At the initial ED visit, tachypnea without hypoxemia and reduced right-sided breath sounds were reported; repeat-visit examination details were not supplied.
Imaging at ED return showed recurrent right pleural effusion.
Repeat thoracentesis on ED return removed 1.2 L of fluid with characteristics similar to the initial milky effusion.

Initial thoracentesis pleural fluid (available as prior record): triglycerides 434 mg/dL, cholesterol 154 mg/dL, 82% lymphocytes, pH 7.48, protein 2.4 g/dL, LDH 83 U/L; cytology without malignant cells.
Initial thoracentesis pleural fluid: Gram stain and culture negative.
CT: bilateral hilar and mediastinal adenopathy, severe right-middle-lobe bronchial narrowing, partial atelectasis and infiltrates.
Bronchoscopy with endobronchial ultrasound guided biopsy established extensive-stage small cell lung carcinoma.
Much later, during febrile deterioration, blood cultures grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

critical: Large symptomatic recurrent pleural effusion requiring drainage and etiologic evaluation

cond: Acceptable if recurrent symptomatic effusion or malignancy workup requires admission; source unit not specified.
Only if clinically stable with expedited drainage/workup and safe follow-up; requires physician adjudication.

facts.v: Woman in her 60s with one week of dyspnea and new nonproductive cough.
Rheumatoid arthritis and stable connective-tissue-disease-associated interstitial lung disease for five years; asbestos-material exposure.
Stable baricitinib and methotrexate regimen.
Hypoxemic, requiring 4 L/min nasal oxygen for saturation >92%; diminished left basal breath sounds and diffuse fine inspiratory crackles; other vitals normal.
No palpable lymph nodes or hepatosplenomegaly.
Mild thrombocytosis; inflammatory markers not significantly elevated; liver, thyroid and kidney tests unremarkable.
Moderate to large homogeneous left pleural effusion.
Postcontrast chest CT: moderate left effusion and nodular circumferential pleural thickening, including mediastinal pleura.
High-volume thoracentesis: atypical epithelioid and spindle cells; SOX10, Melan-A and S100 positive; calretinin, EMA, p40 and WT1 negative.
CT-guided pleural biopsy confirmed cells positive for SOX10 and Melan-A.
Dermatologic and ocular examinations found no suspicious primary lesion.
PET: intensely FDG-avid circumferential pleural disease; no cutaneous or subcutaneous primary identified.
BRAF and KIT wild type.

facts.v: Mild pigmentation over finger joints and knees; no fever, night sweats or cough.
Remote hospitalization for a chest opacity five years earlier without TB diagnosis or treatment; no glucocorticoid use or family hereditary disease history.
Mild pigmentation of hand interphalangeal joints and knees.
Earlier ACTH 577.10 ng/L and cortisol 161.00 nmol/L; admission ACTH 365.80 ng/L and cortisol 139.00 nmol/L.
Low fasting glucose and sodium were described, without numerical values.
T-SPOT.TB positive.
CT: bilateral adrenal nodules with calcification; old tuberculosis lesions in lungs and pleura.
Bilateral hypoechoic adrenal nodules with calcifications; largest left lesion about 2.7 × 2.2 cm; low-intensity enhancement.
Ultrasound-guided left adrenal biopsy: necrotizing granulomatous inflammation. Acid-fast and silver stains negative.
Mycobacterium tuberculosis qPCR detected DNA in adrenal biopsy tissue.

critical: Primary adrenal insufficiency with risk of adrenal crisis

cond: Acceptable for adrenal crisis risk, unstable patient or initiation of complex therapy; not a documented source unit.
Potentially acceptable only after stability, glucocorticoid replacement, crisis education and reliable endocrine/TB follow-up; clinician review required.

facts.v: Four days of progressive jaundice and dark stools with lethargy and lightheadedness; no reported bleeding, fever, cough or abdominal pain.
Advanced lung adenocarcinoma with adrenal and subdiaphragmatic metastases; high tumor PD-L1 expression.
First pembrolizumab 400 mg IV dose 14 days before presentation.
Gastritis, hyperlipidemia, previous cholecystectomy; former smoker.
Afebrile, pale and deeply icteric; HR 92/min, RR 20/min, systolic BP 115 mm Hg.
Hemoglobin 45 g/L, down from 123 g/L baseline.
LDH 1214 U/L, haptoglobin <0.3 g/L, total bilirubin 61 µmol/L with 72% unconjugated; reticulocytes 261.7×10^9/L (23.7%).
Lactate 4.2 mmol/L.
Peripheral blood film: reticulocytosis, spherocytes and reactive neutrophilia.
Direct antiglobulin test IgG 2+ and complement C3d 5+; indirect antiglobulin test panreactive, no underlying alloantibodies detected.
Triple-phase CT abdomen/pelvis found no hemorrhage or intra-abdominal collection.

No trauma, heavy lifting, fever, recent vaccination, chronic illness, known anticoagulant or other prior medication use.
Alert, GCS 15; leg strength 0/5, arm strength 5/5, absent perianal sensation, preserved bulbocavernosus reflex.
Vital signs described as stable; no numerical values reported.
WBC 13,000/µL with 85% neutrophils; platelets 250,000/µL.
PT 12 s, INR 1.0, aPTT 30 s, fibrinogen 300 mg/dL.
Brain and brainstem MRI normal.
Cervicothoracic spine MRI: epidural hematoma compressing the cord and posterior thecal sac from C6 to T2; no traumatic or structural lesion described.
Emergency hemilaminotomy/laminotomy with epidural hematoma evacuation.

facts.v: Progressive diffuse abdominal pain, distension and nausea.
Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, chronic atrial fibrillation and COPD.
ERCP for choledocholithiasis one year earlier, with 10F × 10 cm plastic biliary stent left after stone extraction.
Signs of peritoneal irritation.
Upright abdominal radiograph: multiple small-bowel air–fluid levels.
CT: multiple small-bowel air–fluid levels and a linear hyperdense intraluminal structure consistent with a foreign body; mechanical obstruction suspected.

Emergency laparoscopy converted to open operation because of purulent fluid and adhesions. A Meckel diverticulum ~40 cm proximal to ileocecal valve contained a biliary stent; its distal end perforated adjacent ileum.
About 20 cm of small bowel, including diverticulum and perforation, was resected with side-to-side anastomosis, irrigation and drainage.

critical: Small-bowel obstruction with perforation or peritonitis requiring emergency surgery

cond: Appropriate immediate destination from acute evaluation for perforation/peritonitis.

Amenorrhea and positive home urine pregnancy test; approximately five weeks gestation by dates, gravida 1 para 0.
No reported chronic medical or surgical disease, pelvic inflammatory disease, tobacco or alcohol use.
BP 107/77 mm Hg, HR 89/min, temperature 36.7°C.
Left upper abdominal tenderness; no lower abdominal tenderness, guarding or rigidity; no vaginal bleeding; cervix closed; no palpable adnexal mass or cervical motion tenderness.
Serum hCG 10,130.28 IU/L.

Resected lesion and partial omentum contained products of conception on pathology.
